components.goal: Obtain a sound normal certificate after distance reduction.
components.key_estimate: A_p=(2p+1)3^p/p!; ||y-x||<=3r; ||G(y)+n||<=A_p Lp r^p. The complete correction proof is included in the linked BaseTrial theorem.
components.name: Full evaluated Taylor-model correction
components.operation: At x query the full jet, solve equation (4.1) with the full Taylor polynomial and beta=2Lp/(p-1)!, construct n=-Gbar_x(y)-beta||y-x||^(p-1)(y-x), and evaluate G(y).
components.requires: Known compact convex X and admissible monotone G. The estimate additionally requires ||x-z_star||<=r.
transfer_checks: Retain the original domain X and its outward normal cone.
For approximate models, separately establish normal validity and numerical residual error.
Do not infer a certificate from the halving average without this correction and evaluated test.

content.family: Certified radius trial built from tensor-extragradient halving

limitations.statement: A false radius may return Failure. This routine alone does not supply the unknown-distance guarantee of the separate AdaptiveStrong wrapper.
The finite-schedule and sound-certificate claims do not validate an incorrect strong-monotonicity or smoothness assumption.

performance_links.scope_note: Unnumbered equation (4.12)+Algorithm 2 guarantee; includes valid-radius success and finite false-promise soundness.

variants.cost: At most 2 sum_{j=0}^{J-1}T_p(R/2^j,mu)+2 unknown-G queries, including the final certificate evaluation. This finite cap holds for false radius promises as well. It is O_p(1+(Lp R^(p-1)/mu)^(2/(p+1))+log_+(A_p Lp R^p/delta)), where log_+(s)=max{0,log s} and constants depend only on fixed p. For known affine G(u)=F(u)+a u+b, each G-jet/evaluation uses one original-F jet plus known affine data: add a u+b to the value, aI to the Jacobian, and nothing to higher derivatives. All descendant and certificate evaluations are charged. Internal exact model solving/projection costs are not arithmetic/bit-complexity claims.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Algorithm 2 p.15; equation (4.12) pp.14–15; Section 3.2 p.9.
variants.name: BaseTrial(G,w,mu,R,delta)
variants.output: Failure or an evaluated original-domain certificate: y in X, n in N_X(y), known G(y), ||G(y)+n||<=delta. A valid initial distance promise guarantees the certificate branch.
public_inputs: Known nonempty compact convex original X subset R^d with diam(X)<=D, d>=1, D>0
w in X, fixed integer p>=2, known Lp>0, mu>0, proposed R>0, delta>0
variants.query_and_update: While A_p Lp r^p>delta, set z=Halve(G,z,mu,r), then r=r/2. Halve is Algorithm 1, fully reconstructed in alg.arxiv2609_13462.halve. After the loop query the jet at z; form Gbar_z(y)=sum_{j=0}^{p-1}D^jG(z)[y-z]^j/j!; with b_p=2p/p! and beta=b_p Lp=2Lp/(p-1)!, solve 0 in Gbar_z(y)+beta||y-z||^(p-1)(y-z)+N_X(y). Set n=-Gbar_z(y)-beta||y-z||^(p-1)(y-z); evaluate G(y). If ||G(y)+n||<=delta return (y,n,G(y)); otherwise return Failure.
variants.requirements: Euclidean norm and induced multilinear norm. G is C^(p-1) on a neighborhood of X, mu-strongly monotone on X, and Lip(D^(p-1)G)<=Lp. Use exact known-domain projection and Taylor-model VI computation. No lower-derivative bound is assumed. Radius validity ||w-z_star||<=R is required for guaranteed success, not for sound acceptance or finite scheduling.
variants.state_and_initialization: z=w; r=R; A_p=(2p+1)3^p/p!. The true unique solution z_star and actual distance are hidden; R is supplied and may be false.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Each Halve uses T_p(r,mu)=max{1,ceil([2b_p(4/3)^((p-1)/2)Lp r^(p-1)/mu]^(2/(p+1)))}. The outer loop stops at its explicit radius threshold, irrespective of the unknown true distance. J=max{0,ceil(log_2(A_p Lp R^p/delta)/p)} halving calls are scheduled.

summary: Runs finitely scheduled distance halvings followed by an evaluated model correction. A valid radius guarantees success; a false radius may fail but cannot produce an accepted false certificate.
title: BaseTrial: finite certificate-tested radius trial
use_when: A strongly monotone solver must test a proposed initial distance radius.
Use a separate adaptive wrapper when no radius is supplied; BaseTrial alone does not remove that input.
